text:
jin: hi team, first-day question — i cloned the repo and opened the VS Code devcontainer. `.tool-versions` is present but `asdf current` inside the container says 'no version set'. the same `asdf install` works on my laptop, so i think the container isn't loading my dotfiles or shims. anyone seen this with devcontainers? :wave:

lucy: hey! yep painful but common. devcontainer shells often start non-login, non-interactive. make sure the Dockerfile in .devcontainer installs asdf and adds `~/.asdf/shims` to PATH, and that the entrypoint or shellrc sources `asdf` init. i usually add to container's `/etc/profile.d/asdf.sh`: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` and `eval "$(asdf init -)"`.

jin: ah OK — the devcontainer uses a base image that has asdf installed but no init in /etc/profile.d. i added the file but still my editor tasks can't find node. tasks run with `/bin/sh -c` and fail.

dave: tasks using `/bin/sh -c` will use dash, not zsh, and might skip rc. you can force tasks to run with your login shell by setting the task's `options.shell` in .vscode/tasks.json: `"shell": { "executable": "/bin/bash", "args": ["-lc"] }`. that makes sure bash sources /etc/profile.d. alternatively wrap commands in `bash -lc 'source /etc/profile && node -v'`.

lucy: another gotcha: if your repo uses direnv or a dotfiles bootstrap that symlinks things into the container at runtime, those symlinks might be created as root during image build. check ownership of ~/.asdf and shims. `chown -R vscode:vscode ~/.asdf` inside container can fix it.

jin: thanks. the container image is built in CI as part of the repo. is it better to preinstall the asdf-managed versions in the image instead of relying on runtime `asdf install`?

dave: both approaches work. Preinstalling makes start-up snappy but you must rebuild the image when `.tool-versions` changes. Running `asdf install` on container start is slower but mirrors dev reproducibility. We do a hybrid: CI builds the image and runs `asdf install` during image build (so images have versions) and the entrypoint runs a quick check `asdf current || asdf install --skip-existing`.

jin: ok will try that. one more thing: our infra team also uses Nix on dev machines and some contributors installed nix inside container, which seems to conflict with asdf shims — PATH order flickers. any advice keeping them playing nice?

lucy: keep PATH deterministic in the container. put `/etc/profile.d/99-toolchain.sh` with explicit order, e.g. `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.local/bin:/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin:$PATH"`. also avoid modifying PATH later in user rc files; use `env` in devcontainer.json to set process env too: `"remoteEnv": { "PATH": "/home/vscode/.asdf/shims:/home/vscode/.local/bin:/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin" }`.

dave: if you want to be extra safe, create a tiny wrapper script `/usr/local/bin/node` that execs the asdf shim via `exec $HOME/.asdf/shims/node "$@"` so tasks that call `node` find the right binary even if PATH isn't perfect.

jin: nice. last bit — secrets/tokens in devcontainer: bootstrap tries to load ~/.local.env but it's obviously not in repo. what's recommended so new hires can bring their secrets securely?

lucy: we use 1Password CLI in the container. add `op` to the image and document `op signin` in the onboarding README. devcontainer features can forward the host auth socket but that's advanced. otherwise keep a gitignored `~/.local.env` and a README snippet with `op item get "redwood-dev-tokens" --field NPM_TOKEN > ~/.local.env` steps.

ops-bot: onboarding note: added devcontainer-asdf checklist to internal KB: https://internal.redwood/docs/onboarding/devcontainer-asdf (includes PATH ordering, image-build vs runtime install, and notes about Nix).

jin: amazing, thanks! i'll try adding /etc/profile.d and adjusting tasks.json then report back. :raised_hands:
